maker.match: Match each console to the company that made it.
maker.odd: Three of these consoles were made by {value}. Which one was not?

rows.label: PlayStation 2
rows.description: Sony's second home video game console, part of the sixth generation of consoles
rows.hook: became the best-selling home console of all time and doubled as an affordable DVD player

rows.label: PlayStation 4
rows.description: Sony's fourth home video game console, part of the eighth generation of consoles
rows.hook: launched with a share button on its controller and went head to head with a rival black box

rows.label: PlayStation 3
rows.description: video game console developed Sony Interactive Entertainment
rows.hook: packed a Blu-ray drive and a pricey launch tag, with a famously powerful but tricky Cell chip

rows.label: PlayStation
rows.description: 1994 5th generation video game console by Sony Interactive Entertainment
rows.hook: made CD-based games mainstream and introduced Crash Bandicoot and Final Fantasy VII to a huge audience

rows.label: Xbox Series X and Series S
rows.description: home video game consoles developed by Microsoft
rows.hook: is a pair of sibling consoles, one powerful and one smaller and cheaper, sold side by side

rows.label: Nintendo Entertainment System
rows.description: third generation home video game console
rows.hook: revived home gaming after the crash, bringing Mario and Zelda to living rooms in a gray box

rows.label: PlayStation Portable
rows.description: handheld game console by Sony
rows.hook: let players take near-console-quality 3D games on the go, using small optical discs

rows.label: Nintendo DS
rows.description: Nintendo handheld game console
rows.hook: flipped open like a clamshell with two screens, one of them touch-sensitive and used with a stylus

rows.label: Nintendo 3DS
rows.description: portable 3D dual-screen handheld by Nintendo
rows.hook: showed 3D images on its top screen without needing any special glasses

rows.label: Nintendo GameCube
rows.description: sixth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: was a purple cube-shaped console with a carrying handle and tiny discs, home to Luigi's Mansion and Melee

rows.label: Nintendo 64
rows.description: fifth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: had a three-pronged controller with an analog stick and ran Mario's first 3D adventure

rows.label: Game Boy
rows.description: 1989 portable video game console
rows.hook: was a gray handheld with a green-tinted screen that made Tetris a worldwide obsession

rows.label: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
rows.description: fourth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: gave players a four-button controller with shoulder triggers and hosted Mario World and Donkey Kong Country

rows.label: Sega Genesis
rows.description: fourth-generation home video game console developed by Sega
rows.hook: was the rival console whose speedy blue hedgehog mascot took on the plumber in the early 1990s

rows.label: Dreamcast
rows.description: sixth-generation home video game console developed by Sega
rows.hook: was the last console from its maker and was the first to come with a built-in modem for online play

rows.label: Game Boy Advance
rows.description: handheld game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: was a wider handheld with a landscape layout and shoulder buttons that played Pokemon Ruby and Sapphire

rows.label: PlayStation Vita
rows.description: portable game console developed by Sony Computer Entertainment
rows.hook: offered a handheld with a big OLED screen and a rear touch panel, but needed pricey proprietary memory cards

rows.label: Wii U
rows.description: eighth-generation home video game console by Nintendo
rows.hook: packed a controller with a built-in touchscreen in the middle, as a follow-up to a motion-controlled hit

rows.label: Sega Saturn
rows.description: home video game console
rows.hook: was a 32-bit machine that lost the console race against a gray rival despite a strong arcade lineup

rows.label: Atari 2600
rows.description: home video game console by Atari
rows.hook: popularized home gaming with wood-grain paneling, a joystick and cartridges like Pitfall and Space Invaders

rows.label: Game Boy Color
rows.description: handheld Nintendo video game console introduced in 1998
rows.hook: brought a full palette of hues to a pocket-sized handheld, still playing the older monochrome games

rows.label: TurboGrafx-16
rows.description: fourth-generation home video game console
rows.hook: was a rival to the big-name 8-bit and 16-bit machines that squeezed games onto credit-card-sized cards

rows.label: Neo Geo
rows.description: cartridge-based arcade system board and home video game console developed by SNK
rows.hook: brought arcade-perfect fighting games like Metal Slug and King of Fighters home at a luxury price

rows.label: Virtual Boy
rows.description: table-top video game console developed by Nintendo
rows.hook: was a red-and-black headset-style system showing only red graphics and was a quick commercial flop

rows.label: Game Gear
rows.description: handheld game console developed by Sega
rows.hook: was a full-color handheld rival to a gray brick that guzzled batteries and could become a TV tuner
